subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or remain limited to per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: The requested fix adds or redefines a public operator security/config surface for scheduled autonomous runs, so automation should not choose the precedence and default semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, define precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, and cover message delivery behavior in tests and docs.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as covered by `tools.subagents.tools` with explicit documentation and tests showing the shared semantics.

options.title: Keep per-job controls only
options.body: Decline a global cron policy and document `--tools` plus delivery safeguards as the supported mitigation for duplicate or unsafe message sends.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, define precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, and cover message delivery behavior in tests and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across scoped capability profiles, cron session behavior, and the prior maintainer-facing review on this issue.
